Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Longitudinal chromatin accessibility after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., TNF, EGF, or wounding) transiently, then perform ATAC-seq/CUT&Tag for AP-1 factors (FOS, JUN), H3K27ac, and H3K4me1 at days 0, 1, 7, and 28 after washout. Persistent AP-1-motif-enriched accessible regions in the absence of ongoing signaling, versus naive cells, would indicate memory.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation to separate maintenance from initiation
ideas.description: Use degron tags (dTAG/AID) on JUN/FOS or ATF family members, or a dominant-negative like A-FOS, at different times: before the priming stimulus, during the memory phase, and before re-stimulation. Compare chromatin state and transcriptional response to determine whether AP-1 is required to establish memory, to maintain it, or to execute faster re-induction.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation kinetics and single-cell heterogeneity
ideas.description: Compare primed versus naive cells upon second stimulus using time-resolved scRNA-seq, nascent RNA (PRO-seq/TT-seq), and live reporters of AP-1 target genes. Faster, stronger, or more frequent induction in primed cells that depends on AP-1 binding site integrity would show memory, and single-cell data can distinguish stable bistable states from graded changes.

ideas.title: Targeted enhancer editing and synthetic AP-1 recruitment
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers, and conversely use dCas9-based tethering of FOS/JUN to a naive locus. Test if motif loss abolishes retained accessibility and primed response, and whether forced AP-1 recruitment alone is sufficient to create a lasting, heritable open state after the tether is removed.

ideas.title: Mitotic retention and inheritance across divisions
ideas.description: Track AP-1 occupancy and accessibility through mitosis and across multiple cell divisions using mitotic-synchronized CUT&Tag, live-cell imaging of tagged JUN/FOS, and lineage-tracked sister cells. Mitotic bookmarking by AP-1 and similar memory in sister cells would show it is heritable, and in vivo tests such as inflammation-primed epithelial or stem cells could test physiological relevance.
